name: Choose and execute a registered query
summary: Jev selects an offered query; delegated preparation and system validation produce executable inputs.

steps.label: Choose the offered query
steps.human:
Consider each query’s purpose, supported questions, required and optional inputs, output fields, source scope, completeness meaning and known limits.

A query is self-describing: for example, an AC-family query accepts a family ID plus population rule and returns attributable AC rows, work status and coverage limits. A title alone is not enough.

Illustrative input contract: family_id (required canonical ID), inclusion (root-excluded or terminal leaves), levels (optional). Output contract: AC records with canonical_id, work_status, source locator/revision; complete flag, known_count, exact_total only when complete, and limitations. These are conceptual catalog semantics, not a new wire schema. Choose the offered query ID/version and its contract, or a bounded none/clarify outcome. Only a selected query continues to input preparation.

I/O boundary: Illustrative successful selection uses the same example_ac_requirements descriptor and choice ID. Existing ChoiceAnswer is reusable transport; target catalog orchestration remains proposed.

steps.label: Bind known values or dispatch preparation
steps.human:
Copy trusted known values, or construct a typed host request with question, query/version, contract and approved context. Persist the matching wait. Retrieval-specific preparation binding is proposed; existing host transport is reused. Terms-only help does not execute the full search child; choosing full search transfers ownership directly to shared attempt comparison.

I/O boundary: Only reusable transport fields are shown; operation and output_schema_id are intentionally not fabricated. Without that missing binding this is not dispatchable.
